papers.title: LM6-CastBench: A Geometry-Aware Simulation Dataset for Transient Thermal Prediction in LM6 Sand Casting
papers.abstract: Transient thermal fields during solidification connect casting process conditions and cooling behaviour to the formation of defect-prone regions in aluminum cast ings. Repeatedly solving this thermal problem across geometries and process conditions is computationally expensive, motivating data-driven surrogate models. However, existing machine-learning studies on casting thermal behaviour rely on study-specific simulation databases that do not support reproducible geometry-level benchmarking. We introduce LM6-CastBench, an open simulation dataset for geometry-aware learning of transient thermal fields in LM6 aluminum sand casting, combining three geometry families, ten variants per family, five pouring tempera tures, and three mould temperatures (450 geometry-process cases in total). Each case retains CAD geometry, unstructured mesh connectivity, spatial descriptors, process metadata, and time-resolved nodal temperatures. We benchmark a point wise MLP against a spatially structured U-Net under geometry-level data splits; the U-Net reduces temperature-field errors by a large margin, with the biggest gains on geometries with localized features and abrupt section changes. LM6-CastBench gives researchers a reproducible dataset and benchmark for geometry-aware surro gate modelling of casting thermal behaviour.

papers.title: Autonomous Analysis of Thermoelectric Materials Big Data by Multi-Agentic AI and Construction of a Knowledge Base and Specialized AI
papers.abstract: Extracting knowledge from large databases of experimental materials data requires repeated analyses and reusable records of their choices and results. We developed Multi-Agentic AI (MAA), a multi-agent system in which AI agents with distinct roles analyze experimental thermoelectric data under predefined instructions and quality checks, saving analysis records traceable to their sources. In four experiments varying theme and cycle counts, we measured what accumulated in these records. In the largest experiment (100 analyses across 10 themes and 10 cycles), concept co-occurrences were concentrated within themes, vocabulary was shared across themes and some relation descriptions were first detected in later cycles. A specialized AI that searches this experiment's knowledge bases and reads their analysis records answered materials questions with cited sources. Retrospective checks, including tracing an answer generated with a preliminary corpus back to the source data, exposed errors: traceability makes errors findable but not absent.

papers.title: Beyond Synthesis Conditions: Linking In-situ Growth Dynamics to Carbon Nanotube Forest Properties through Multimodal Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Machine learning for chemical vapor deposition (CVD) of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) has largely mapped static synthesis conditions to final properties, implicitly treating these conditions as a complete description of growth. Here, we test this assumption by integrating gas-flow conditions with in-situ time-resolve growth profiles (growth curves) of vertically aligned CNT forests. We introduce an observation-window analysis, in which prediction is evaluated as a function of observation time by providing models with the growth curve only up to progressively later times, to determine not only whether a property can be predicted, but when the necessary information becomes available during synthesis. Clustering of normalized growth curves revealed distinct growth patterns independent of final forest height. The gas conditions alone could predict the initial growth rate but not the growth lifetime and failed to capture the variation in yield (R^2<0). Adding the growth curve improved yield prediction (R^2~0.4-0.5), with the relevant information emerging during the intermediate and later stages of growth rather than at its onset. In contrast, density and G/D ratio, which forest height does not record, showed no consistent improvement. The maximum height and lifetime could be estimated with moderate accuracy midway through the 10-min growth. Permutation feature importance identified water vapor and H_2, both linked to catalyst activity, as the most informative gas variables. These results indicate that variation unexplained by synthesis conditions is not merely noise but reflects an evolving catalyst state, and they establish mid-growth decision points for autonomous synthesis, enabling early termination of unpromising batches and, ultimately, in-batch adjustment of growth conditions.

papers.title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
papers.abstract: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

papers.title: PaddleMaterials: An End-to-End Deep Learning Toolkit for Materials Science
papers.abstract: Machine learning supports materials design, atomistic simulation and experimental characterization, yet models and workflows remain fragmented. We present PaddleMaterials, an open-source framework integrating heterogeneous materials-learning tasks while preserving task-specific representations and scientific semantics. It unifies data processing, training, evaluation, pretrained-model management and workflows across six task classes: property prediction, structure generation, machine-learning interatomic potentials, electronic-structure fields, spectrum elucidation and microscopy image processing. Task interfaces record physical quantities, units, aggregation conventions and references, making cross-task composition verifiable. A shared compiler backend enables switching from dynamic-graph to compiled execution through one setting, using graph optimization, operator fusion and hardware-targeted code generation without changing model definitions. Across 65 model instances in 11 groups, compiled execution accelerated every instance in eight groups, with group median speedups of 11%-224% and group maximum speedups of 11%-336%. Case studies on LiMnO2 and toluene link structure generation or spectrum elucidation, interatomic-potential relaxation, property prediction and electron-density prediction, using same-geometry density functional theory (DFT) calculations as references. For LiMnO2, predicted formation energies for generated and relaxed structures differed from same-geometry PBE+U references by at most 7 meV per atom, while the computational cost of model steps was less than one-twentieth of a DFT single-point calculation. PaddleMaterials extends unified materials workflows beyond conventional property, potential and structure-generation tasks while supporting verifiable cross-task operations and compiled execution.

papers.title: InformedXRD: Reproducible Benchmarks and Physics-Informed Evaluation for Powder Diffraction Symmetry Classification
papers.abstract: Machine learning for powder diffraction (PXRD) symmetry classification is being trained at scale, yet the field lacks a common evaluation standard: papers report results on different subsets of experimental archives, with different target taxonomies, preprocessing, and metrics, and published models are rarely released in a form that permits rescoring. We present InformedXRD, an evaluation framework with three parts: (i) a machine-readable mapping from 230 space groups to 99 extinction groups, the finest classes powder diffraction can identify from systematic absences alone; (ii) a benchmark-construction method whose inclusion rules are specified as code and reproduce from a frozen snapshot, instantiated as RRUFF-473, RRUFF-325, and, as a small example, opXRD-98; (iii) a reporting protocol with prior-only frequency baselines, a label-permutation test, a hierarchy-aware error metric on the condensed translationengleiche subgroup graph, and stratified evaluation. We build on the mapping, RRUFF benchmarks, subgroup graph, and four ViT checkpoints released in our earlier work (Baggett et al., 2026). Using these checkpoints, a 1D residual CNN, and six architectures trained under the XRDBench recipe (Cao et al., 2025), we show that evaluation design changes what conclusions are justified: paired tests point in different directions at Top-1 and Top-5; paired Top-k tests do not separate the three leading XRDBench models, while hierarchy-aware analysis describes error distance and direction across all six; an input-blind frequency predictor matches the models on aggregate Top-k, yet a label-permutation test still detects pattern-specific evidence; and stratified analysis exposes a label-entropy confound that aggregate accuracy hides. All mapping tables, benchmark code, scripts, and checkpoints are released as shared infrastructure for PXRD-ML evaluation.

papers.title: Organizational Learning in Materials Discovery Campaigns: Which Databases, Calculations, and Agent Teams Pay Off
papers.abstract: More databases can make a materials campaign worse. Through an organizational lens, we trace each source's contribution. One band-gap campaign ranks seven anion families from archived measured gaps, one vote per source. In the first half of its budget, all seven pooled rank worse (rank agreement 0.737; 1 = measured order) than the best pool of three (0.851). As a stability check, choosing the pool on half the runs and testing on the rest kept the gap. Splitting Materials Project afterwards points to its transition-metal oxides and fluorides. Two databases from one pipeline add nothing over one, but pooling gives their shared ordering two votes. New calculations repay their cost early only when two or three campaigns reuse them. Flat language-model agent teams trailed a random-pick baseline (mean 0.876, sd 0.096, 20 searches). An adaptive Al-Mg-Si team, mostly interatomic potentials, was scored on unseen HSE06 calculations. In its first quarter of compute it found 49% of the ten lowest-formation-energy compounds, against at most 40% for fixed teams and 73% for MACE-MP-0 alone. Merging members whose orderings agreed carried most of its gain. This suggests pooling a few sources that fit the measurements, counting each pipeline once and charging for computation.

papers.title: Accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth via tensor decomposition
papers.abstract: Phase-field models provide a powerful framework for simulating grain growth phenomena in polycrystalline materials, but their application to large-scale systems is limited by the high computational and memory costs associated with resolving multiple phase variables over fine spatial and temporal scales. This paper presents a tensor decomposition based model reduction framework for accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth. The proposed method exploits the underlying low-rank structure of the evolving phase-field variables and represents the high-dimensional solution in a spatially decomposed tensor format. By performing the numerical computations directly within this reduced representation, the framework decreases storage requirements and reduces the cost of repeatedly solving the phase-field equations. The number of modes for the decomposed approximation is controlled during the online computation with a subspace mode-updating algorithm, to balance computational efficiency and approximation accuracy. The method is assessed using representative grain growth problems, and its predictions are compared with those obtained from conventional full-order finite element simulations. The results demonstrate that the formulation can accurately reproduce the evolution of grain morphology and the principal characteristics of grain growth kinetics while substantially improving computational efficiency. The proposed framework therefore provides a promising approach for extending phase-field simulations to larger spatial domains, finer discretizations, and systems containing a large number of phase variables.

papers.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
papers.abstract: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

papers.title: Programmable Droplets as Active Matter in a Reconfigurable Environment
papers.abstract: Exploring systems that bridge the gap between non living and living matter requires a reconfigurable environment coupled to synthetic systems capable of autonomous motion, adaptive behaviour and persistent dynamics. Self propelled droplets provide a minimal platform for such life like behaviour, but quantitative measures capturing both persistence and adaptability to enable closed loop reconfiguration remain lacking. Here we introduce an autonomous closed loop robotic platform to characterise and dynamically program the autonomous behaviour of multicomponent oil in water droplets. We explored two chemical composition spaces, with and without external pH perturbations, analysing droplet behaviour in real time and iteratively selecting formulations. To quantify this behaviour, we introduce two descriptors, persistence and diversity. Persistence is quantified by mapping temporal dynamics in a speed shape complexity space, where we identify a persistence domain that distinguishes active from inactive droplets. Diversity captures spontaneous or environmentally induced variation in motion and the propensity of droplets to reorient or adapt under perturbation. We show that persistence and diversity are constrained by a behavioural trade off: high persistence limits diversity, whereas high diversity reduces persistent activity. Our results provide a quantitative framework for navigating and programming life like behaviours in active droplets and show how closed-loop experimentation can uncover organising principles in complex active matter.

papers.title: Compatibility of Martensitic Microstructures in Polycrystals
papers.abstract: The paper studies martensitic microstructures in polycrystals, focussing on their compatibility across grain boundaries. After a reduction to the case of a planar grain boundary, the case when the grain boundary separates two constant gradients of zero energy is considered. It is shown that for cubic-to tetragonal transformations such a configuration can occur when the relative grain rotation is not in the cubic group. Then the case when the grain boundary separates two simple laminates of zero energy is considered, it being shown using a computer-assisted symbolic calculation that in the cubic-to-tetragonal case compatibility is only possible for a closed set of measure zero in the manifold of grain boundary normals and relative grain rotations, and that a similar slightly weaker result holds for cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations. The results suggest why higher-order laminates are often observed for such transformations. The Taylor set of deformation gradients is defined and studied, this set having the property that any deformation whose gradient belongs to it corresponds to a zero-energy microstructure for the polycrystal independent of grain geometry and grain rotations. New upper bounds for the Taylor set are proved for cubic-to-tetragonal and cubic-to-orthorhombic transformations, generalizing those of Bhattacharya and Kohn using the geometrically linearized theory. We give a simple proof of a related result of Peigney characterizing the positive diagonal matrices in the quasiconvex hull of the energy wells for cubic-to-tetragonal transformations.

papers.title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
papers.abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

papers.title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Current methods of deriving ultrastiff isotropic metamaterials require heuristics or topology optimization, which are highly inefficient and limited by human input. To circumvent this, Physics Informed Neural Networks are applied to analytical equations to systematically solve for plate orientations in closed cell lattices. Following a standardized procedure, the plate orientations were modelled and assembled into geometries resembling quasi random foams for validation via finite element simulations. Closed cell 6-plate geometries were also additively manufactured using LAPIS and experimentally characterized. The results indicate that a minimum of 6 plates is required to constitute an ultrastiff isotropic lattice, 7 plates would return the established plate Cubic Octet structure while 8 to 10 plate geometries did not show significant differences in properties. Despite the introduction of some plate bending due to sub-optimal plate placement strategy, relative stiffness of the PINNs lattices adheres closely to the Hashin Shtrikman upper bound, 90 percent of Hashin Shtrikman upper bound at a relative density of 0.4, and the lattices maintain near isotropic behaviour, achieving a Zener ratio of 0.95 at a relative density of 0.1. Benchmarking results show that specific stiffness of PINNs lattices is higher than the majority of isotropic architectures reported in the literature.

papers.title: Optical Signature of Bias-Induced Carrier Injection in a WSe2/MoS2 Heterostructure Diode
papers.abstract: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructure diode. Under forward bias, trion-related emission in WSe$_2$ is markedly enhanced, whereas reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.

papers.title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes in optical response across the chalcogen series. The absorption onset shifts toward lower photon energies, from approximately 2.4 eV in Y2CdS4 to 1.7 eV in Y2CdTe4. Thermoelectric calculations indicate promising Seebeck coefficients and power factors, with Y2CdSe4 exhibiting a favorable balance of transport properties. Charge-density distributions, electron localization functions, and Bader charge analyses suggest increasing covalent bonding contributions from sulfide to telluride. These findings highlight the potential of Y2CdX4 compounds for tunable optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications.

papers.title: On-the-fly $\Delta$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
papers.abstract: We develop a framework for on-the-fly $\Delta$-machine learned force field ($\Delta$-MLFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of warm dense matter (WDM). In particular, we employ a Yukawa reference model that captures the dominant screened-Coulomb interactions between the ions, with its parameters fit on the fly to Kohn--Sham density functional theory (DFT) data, and an MLFF scheme based on the kernel method and Bayesian linear regression that learns the differences in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses between the Yukawa model and Kohn--Sham DFT. We verify the accuracy and performance of the formalism by comparing the predicted properties of warm dense carbon with Kohn--Sham DFT results in the literature. In so doing, we demonstrate that $\Delta$-MLFF has significantly lower errors in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses than the standard MLFF scheme at a comparable cost, while accelerating ab initio MD simulations by up to three orders of magnitude. We apply this framework to calculate the equation of state, structure, and transport properties of magnesium at densities of 5.22 to 10.44 g/cm$^3$ and temperatures of 600 kK to 1.5 MK. We find that the pressure, self-diffusion coefficient, and shear viscosity obey power laws in temperature and density, that the dynamic structure factor exhibits a well-defined ion-acoustic mode whose negative dispersion is characteristic of strongly coupled liquids, and that the Stokes--Einstein relation holds to within 10% over the conditions considered.

papers.title: Fabry-P\'erot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
papers.abstract: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-P\'erot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.

papers.title: In the age of big data and AI: do we still need chemical bonds?
papers.abstract: Chemical bonding is the language through which chemistry rationalizes materials structure, stability, properties, and reactivity. Meanwhile, modern deep-learning models achieve remarkable predictive performance using representations based largely on compositional and structural information, raising the question of whether explicit bonding concepts remain necessary. In this work, we argue that artificial intelligence does not render chemical bonding obsolete but provides a new framework for evaluating and refining bonding concepts. We show that, through linear probing, Allegro and MACE embeddings recover bonding descriptors with (R^2 > 0.95), indicating that bonding emerges naturally from Allegro's and MACE's latent spaces. We also show that bonding descriptors provide information beyond bond distance in our electronic-structure-featurized MEGNet (ESF-MEGNet) model, reducing prediction error for properties including bulk and shear moduli by 15%. We discuss implications for interpretable machine learning, synthesizability prediction, and generative materials design, and suggest joint-embedding approaches for learning more general bonding representations. More broadly, we propose that chemical bonding can be understood as a learnable representation of electronic structure. From this perspective, different bonding models represent alternative compressions of the underlying electronic information and can be evaluated through their predictive power, dimensionality, and complexity. The age of machine learning shifts the focus from whether a bonding model is physically motivated to whether it captures the information required to explain and predict materials behavior. If a materials genome exists, it should be encodable through a representation of chemical bonding. If no bonding representation can capture this information, our understanding of the chemical bond may require revision.

papers.title: Quantum dynamics of ultrasmall magnetic skyrmions in atomic-defect landscapes
papers.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~\AA. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~$\mu$eV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. Saddle points of the energy landscape act as quantum beam splitters for skyrmions, and quantum depinning reaches rates of 1--100~Hz below the critical current. Embedded impurities, in contrast, bind the skyrmion so strongly that it ceases to behave as a rigid particle, defining a strong-coupling regime. For the Gilbert damping typical of ultrathin films, the quantized levels remain well resolved. The thermal-to-quantum crossover lies between 40 and 160~mK, which is within reach of millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy, where tip-induced escape statistics and electron spin resonance STM can reveal the quantized gyrotropic motion of skyrmions pinned at defects crafted atom by atom.

papers.title: Evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
papers.abstract: Correlations and topology are central pillars in the study of emergent electronic phases. Topological flat bands near the Fermi level unite these concepts, providing a route towards correlated topological phenomena and unconventional magnetism. Despite theoretical predictions, momentum-resolved observation of a topological flat band at the Fermi level has remained elusive. Using angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a flat band at the Fermi level within the topologically non-trivial electronic structure of the magnetic kagome Weyl semimetal Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$. We further uncover a strong temperature dependence in which the flat band shifts across the Fermi level, accompanied by a reconstruction of the Fermi surface. Strikingly, this evolution occurs on the same temperature scale as previously reported anomalies in the magnetic response. Together, these results provide evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$, establishing a microscopic setting in which topology, electronic correlations, and magnetism become intertwined.

papers.title: Helical Magnetic Nature of $\beta$-Mn Structured CoZn Thin-Films Determined by a Bayesian Approach to Modeling Polarized Neutron Reflectivity Data
papers.abstract: Chiral magnetic materials can host skyrmions and hence are of interest for numerous spintronic applications including low-power storage. To reach this goal, room temperature operation and a thin film form are needed. We have studied the chiral magnetism in a $\beta$-Mn structured CoZn sputtered film, with a Curie temperature of $\approx 130$ {\deg}C, by means of polarized neutron reflectometry (PNR) in order to reveal its magnetic field-temperature phase diagram. In bulk this material has a helimagnetic ground state. Here we use PNR data to show that the helimagnetism survives in a CoZn film only 100 nm thick, roughly half a helical period. Given the subtlety of differentiating the helical state from a uniform state with reduced interfacial magnetism, we have developed and employed a Bayesian approach that uses model selection to analyze our PNR data and to map out the field-temperature phase diagram of our thin film.

papers.title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
papers.abstract: Borophene, a monolayer of boron, is distinctive among two-dimensional materials owing to its unique properties, including polymorphism and potential applications in quantum technologies and energy conversion and storage. Nevertheless, its applications are hindered by the strong binding of borophene to metal substrates, which impedes the realization of freestanding borophene. Alternative substrates with tunable binding to borophene are therefore highly desirable. Since boride layers arise during borophene synthesis on metals, borides provide potential alternative substrates for borophene synthesis. In this work, we investigate the binding energies and interactions between borophene and 1356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases (v1/6 and v1/9), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML). Importantly, incorporating ML-predicted charge transfer as an input feature to a subsequent ML model enables physics-informed predictions of binding energies. Additional DFT calculations on four representative cases were performed to validate the ML predictions. SHAP analysis reveals that the majority of key descriptors are associated with delocalized electrons, highlighting the role of electronic properties in governing binding strength. Combined DFT and ML screening identifies 65 and 73 promising boride surfaces for the v1/6 and v1/9 phases, respectively. Al- and Ag-based borides, including AlB2 and AgB2, emerge as predominant candidates for both phases. The computationally predicted candidate substrates and the deduced design guidelines provide a charge-transfer-informed ML strategy for substrate selection and represent promising steps toward the experimental realization of freestanding borophene.

papers.title: Elucidating the topological nature of molecular beam epitaxy grown high Curie temperature (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x using angle resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is used to elucidate the band structure of (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x, a new magnetic quantum material grown using molecular beam epitaxy that has a Curie temperature (TC) above 100K, much higher than those reported for other materials of the MnxSb2-xTe4 class. Conflicting and sparse theory and experiments, as well as the complex disordered structure of the materials make it difficult to establish their topological nature. Here we explore this question by performing ARPES studies for two samples with x=0.65 and x=0.92, respectively. Images of the band structures of these two samples were acquired using photon energy dependent studies. The bulk and surface states of this complex material system, and the effects of composition on the band structure were investigated. Evidence of surface state features as well as bulk related ones were obtained, supporting their non-trivial nature. No signature of Fermi-arcs consistent with Weyl semimetals were seen. A shift in the Fermi level of the two samples due to different carrier densities allowed observation of the onset of a Dirac point in the surface states. Temperature dependent ARPES suggests possible band splitting as the materials undergo magnetic transitions, helping to understand the magnetic interactions. Our results point to their likely magnetic topological insulating nature.

papers.title: Heterostructure morphology stability maps in multiphase nanoparticles
papers.abstract: In the rapidly growing field of nanocombinatorics, the advent of megalibraries of multiphase nanoparticles (NPs) has created a need for predictive computational approaches. A notable characteristic of multiphase NPs is the internal interface architecture that arises from the joining of constituent phases at boundaries. We propose a strategy to predict the ground-state interface architecture from the DFT-calculated surface and interfacial energies of all constituent phases as input and use this strategy to create stability maps to predict multiphase NP morphologies. A Potts model, a $q$-state generalization of the Ising model, in which $q-1$ spins represent discretized regions of a constituent phase, provides a flexible, discretized representation of a $(q-1)$-phase nanoparticle with arbitrary interfacial join morphology. Interactions between spins represent interactions between phases, or interfacial energies. To model the surface of a nanoparticle, an additional spin represents the surrounding environment and interaction energies with this spin are surface energies. We apply a Monte Carlo algorithm to search for the lowest-energy spin configuration. The trade-off between surface and interfacial energy minimization drives the formation of an interface morphology. We calculate a biphase nanoparticle interface morphology stability map to study the relation between the three biphase morphologies we found. Next, we use the stability map to predict NP morphologies of sample biphase systems and compare these to experimentally available data. We repeat the grid search approach for triphase nanoparticle interface morphologies and discover 11 triphase morphologies, nine more than previously enumerated. We then predict sample triphase systems and finally revisit experimentally reported triphase morphologies.

papers.title: SeriesXRD: automated reflection tracking and phase identification in high-pressure X-ray diffraction series
papers.abstract: High-pressure synchrotron X-ray diffraction increasingly produces hundreds to thousands of detector frames in a single experiment, while separating, assigning, and tracking weak reflections across an entire series often remain manual. This bottleneck is particularly severe for micron- and nanoscale samples in diamond-anvil cells, where scattering from the anvils, gasket, pressure medium, and pressure markers can dominate the sample signal. We present SeriesXRD, an open-source workflow that analyzes diffraction as a series rather than as independent patterns. The program suppresses azimuthally localized diamond scattering, subtracts background, fits and tracks reflections between frames, matches known phases using pressure-dependent lattice parameters, subtracts confidently assigned contributions, and groups persistent unexplained reflections for follow-up as candidate sample-associated or unknown-phase features. We demonstrate the method on 1288 frames collected from an approximately 30-nm-thick layered UOTe flake in a diamond-anvil cell over 3.5-50.7 GPa. The dataset is strongly background dominated, with detectable UOTe diffraction in only approximately 4% of the frames. SeriesXRD recovered the sample-associated reflections identified in the original manual analysis while reducing the corresponding phase-assignment and residual-analysis workflow from more than two months of researcher time to an overnight automated run. Across the full series, 17,143 peaks were fitted, 14,395 passed quality criteria, and 90% of accepted peaks were assigned to known background or reference phases. SeriesXRD therefore converts large, background-dominated diffraction series into a tractable set of phase assignments and coherent unexplained reflections while retaining a traceable record of each decision.

papers.title: Zeeman Spin Photocurrents without Spin Textures
papers.abstract: Inversion symmetry forbids bulk second-order spin photocurrents driven solely by electric-dipole coupling. We show that interference between the electric-dipole and spin Zeeman couplings of light enables Zeeman spin-shift and spin-injection currents in centrosymmetric magnets. Our microscopic theory and systematic symmetry analysis establish the allowed responses and polarization selection rules for both spin-degenerate and spin-split antiferromagnets, with and without spin--orbit coupling (SOC). In collinear magnets without SOC, spin injection vanishes, whereas a pure spin-shift current survives independently of the carrier scattering time. This response arises from transverse electronic spin coherences generated by the optical magnetic field, while the ordered moments remain collinear and fixed. Model analyses validate the mechanism, and first-principles calculations for $\mathrm{MnF_2}$ predict experimentally accessible spin photocurrents. These findings establish a general framework for optical spin-current generation in centrosymmetric magnets, including a SOC-free pure-spin mechanism particularly relevant to altermagnets.

papers.title: IRIS: an agentic eye on symmetry-derived paths and energy landscapes of structural phase transitions
papers.abstract: Structural phase transitions underpin ferroelectric and multiferroic functionality, but constructing interpretable energy landscapes remains dependent on specialist expertise. Predicting this behaviour rests on Landau free energies expanded in symmetry-adapted order parameters: their coefficients classify a transition, expose the couplings between distortions, set switching paths and barriers, and parametrize phase-field and effective-Hamiltonian models at larger scales. Obtaining these coefficients from first principles means sampling the Born--Oppenheimer energy surface along symmetry-derived structural paths, which requires crystallographic analysis, reliable structure generation and extensive computation, especially for coupled multidimensional order parameters. Here we introduce IRIS, an agentic workflow that converts plain-language requests and crystal structures into symmetry-adapted energy landscapes and fitted Landau energy models. Deterministic gates govern acceptance of structures, calculations and fits, while language models interpret requests and select constrained recovery actions. Applications across six compounds include a six-dimensional BiFeO$_3$ landscape that separates competition between polar and tilt amplitudes from directional locking and ranks homogeneous switching pathways. Controlled replays detected all 53 injected faults; disabling gates allowed 14 silent errors. Four prospective BaTiO$_3$ runs produced fitted landscapes from 96 density-functional calculations in 34 minutes total without intervening human decisions. IRIS makes physical model construction a reusable computational capability and provides a framework for scientific automation grounded in explicit verification.

papers.title: Diffusion-Based Generative Screening of ABX$_3$ Perovskite Compositions for Bandgap-Targeted Materials Discovery
papers.abstract: Crystal-generation models can explore compositions and atomic arrangements beyond a fixed set of crystal prototypes, but their usefulness for a specific materials family depends on whether the generated structures retain the defining topology and whether their predicted properties remain reliable across the sampled chemistry. Here, a pretrained diffusion model is used to generate candidate ABX$_3$ perovskites and to examine their structural, chemical and electronic-property distributions. A connectivity-based filter distinguishes three-dimensional corner-sharing perovskites from structures that share the same nominal ABX$_3$ stoichiometry. The accepted set contains substantial B-site multiplicity, including ordered double-perovskite configurations that are inaccessible to the two-prototype substitution reference used here. The generated set is enriched in chloride-, bromide- and iodide-containing compositions relative to the Materials Project, while all generated B-site elements are already represented in that database. On the downstream MP-trained ALIGNN scale, the predicted bandgap distribution is shifted towards 1.4 eV, but the target-window fraction (8.2\%) is close to the MP reference fraction (7.3\%); the separate MatterGen and ALIGNN label sources prevent this comparison from establishing target-condition enrichment. An ALIGNN model performs well on a formula-grouped random test split but does not outperform a constant baseline on a deliberately severe B-site-disjoint test. First-principles calculations on six generated structures show that relaxation can alter structural classification and that predicted and calculated gaps can differ appreciably. These results identify both the chemical-space coverage offered by crystal diffusion and the structural and predictive checks needed before its outputs can be treated as materials candidates.

papers.title: Radiofrequency plasma spheroidization of lightweight complex concentrated superalloy Al10Nb20Ta15Ti30V5Zr20
papers.abstract: Recent advances in additive manufacturing (AM) have significantly increased the demand for high-quality metal powders with tailored composition. For refractory complex concentrated alloys (RCCA) preparing such powders by conventional metallurgical method remains challenging due to their high melting point and chemical reactivity. In this paper, we present a method to produce spherical RCCA powders (here Al10Nb20Ta15Ti30V5Zr20) via mechanical alloying followed by radio-frequency inductively coupled plasma spheroidization. The resulting powder is suitable for AM processes because of its spherical morphology and a microstructure consisting of major BCC phases with local B2 phase. Complex carbide formation was studied by 3D atom probe tomography.

papers.title: Efficient Interpolation of the Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian at Arbitrary Momenta
papers.abstract: We develop an efficient reciprocal-space method to reconstruct the static Bethe-Salpeter (BSE) Hamiltonian at arbitrary crystal momenta from coarse first-principles grids. Bloch states are interpolated within an optimally smooth Wannier subspace, while the screened Coulomb interaction is reconstructed from the dielectric response. This decouples the electron-hole transition momenta and transferred momentum from the underlying ab initio sampling. We benchmark the method on monolayer hBN, monolayer MoS$_2$, and bulk GaAs against explicit ab initio calculations, finding excellent agreement for dense-grid Bloch states, dielectric screening, and BSE optical spectra. Furthermore, our cost analysis estimates speedups of up to $22\times$ on the grids considered here. Arbitrary transferred-momentum sampling gives direct access to the long-wavelength exciton dispersion: in hBN and MoS$_2$, we resolve the nonanalytic behaviour induced by long-range electron-hole exchange at momenta well below the spacing of practical uniform grids. For bulk GaAs, locally refined transition-momentum sampling yields a converged binding energy for the threefold-degenerate lowest exciton, in close agreement with experiment and reference calculations, using far fewer BSE points than conventional uniform meshes. As the present framework provides exciton energies and amplitudes at arbitrary crystal momenta, it opens the way to incorporating ab initio excitonic effects into nonlocal electron-phonon vertices and to extensions towards exciton-phonon interactions and nonequilibrium exciton dynamics.
